result.summary: Wrote test/specs/REQ-202.md and two ExUnit test files covering all 14 acceptance criteria plus cross-tenant isolation and real Task.async concurrency, following test/letflow/audit_test.exs's tenant-fixture pattern (REQ-195's structural sibling) and test/letflow/definitions/promotion_digest_test.exs's moduledoc-content-assertion pattern (Code.fetch_docs/1). CRITICAL FINDING, not a test-design defect: this suite was actually run against a real Postgres instance available in this environment (docker container letflow-1-postgres-1, port from .env's LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5463) and surfaced TWO real, reproducible implementation defects in the shipped migration/schema, both rooted in the same cause -- an Ecto-default index/constraint name exceeding PostgreSQL's 63-byte identifier limit. See test/specs/REQ-202.md section 1 for full detail, root-cause tracing, and the diagnostic verification method (a temporary local patch, confirmed reverted via git status showing no diff, that isolated Defect A and reproduced Defect B's exact stacktrace). Running the two new test files against the CURRENT, unmodified, committed implementation: 23/38 pass, 15 fail, every failure traced to Defect A (every provisioned_tenant() call in test/letflow/repository_test.exs fails to replay this migration into a real tenant schema). With Defect A alone patched out diagnostically (not committed), 37/38 pass, with the sole remaining failure being Defect B (the concurrent create/2 test), reproduced with its exact Ecto.ConstraintError stacktrace pointing at lib/letflow/repository.ex:153.

defect_a_duplicate_index_name.root_cause: The migration's unique_index/3 call ([:artifact_kind, :artifact_name, :version_number]) and its plain index/3 call ([:artifact_kind, :artifact_name, desc: :version_number]) both resolve to the SAME Ecto default index name (artifact_versions_artifact_kind_artifact_name_version_number_index, 66 chars) because Ecto's default_index_name/1 (deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/migration.ex:1054-1068) strips the desc:/asc: direction wrapper when generating a name.
defect_a_duplicate_index_name.reproduction: Every call to TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/1 against a real, newly provisioned tenant schema fails with Postgrex error 42P07 duplicate_table ("relation ... already exists") -- confirmed directly, not inferred. mix ecto.migrate against the main/dev schema reports success trivially only because this migration's `if prefix() do` guard is false there (prefix() is nil outside a tenant-scoped replay), masking the defect from a plain `mix ecto.migrate` smoke check.
defect_a_duplicate_index_name.impact: The entire REQ-202 feature is currently unusable against any real tenant -- not an edge case. Every one of this suite's 15 tenant-provisioning integration tests fails for this reason against the current committed code.
defect_a_duplicate_index_name.suggested_fix_direction: Give the plain index/3 call (or the unique_index/3 call) an explicit, shorter `name:` option so the two never collide and both fit within Postgres's 63-byte NAMEDATALEN limit. Decision on which one and the exact name is ELIXIR-DEV's, not this handoff's.

defect_b_truncated_constraint_name_misma.root_cause: The same 66-char default name exceeds Postgres's 63-byte identifier limit, so Postgres silently truncates it to artifact_versions_artifact_kind_artifact_name_version_number_in (63 chars) when actually creating the constraint. ArtifactVersion.changeset/2's unique_constraint/3 declares the FULL, untruncated 66-char atom as `name:`, which never matches Postgres's actual (truncated) constraint name.
defect_b_truncated_constraint_name_misma.reproduction: Confirmed via a diagnostic-only local patch (reverted before this handoff -- git status shows no diff on the migration file) that fixed Defect A in isolation, then re-ran the suite: the concurrent create/2 test fails with an unhandled Ecto.ConstraintError (not a caught {:error, changeset}), with a stacktrace pointing at lib/letflow/repository.ex:153 inside create_with_retries/7, which has no rescue clause for it.
defect_b_truncated_constraint_name_misma.impact: Defeats design section 4.4's entire concurrency-retry contract: a genuine unique-constraint violation from two racing create/2 calls is not converted into a changeset error at all -- it crashes the caller instead of retrying. This is exactly the scenario the design's own moduledoc documents as the safety mechanism for concurrent writers.
defect_b_truncated_constraint_name_misma.suggested_fix_direction: Once Defect A's name collision is resolved with an explicit short name, ArtifactVersion.changeset/2's unique_constraint/3 :name option must be updated to the SAME short name used in the migration (both must agree, and both must fit within 63 bytes). ELIXIR-DEV's call on the exact name.

issues: Two real, reproducible implementation defects found in the currently-committed code (priv/repo/migrations/20260830030001_create_repository_artifacts.exs and lib/letflow/repository/artifact_version.ex) -- see result.defects_found above and test/specs/REQ-202.md section 1 for full root-cause detail. RECOMMENDATION: ORCH should route this back to ELIXIR-DEV for a rework cycle (fixing both index/constraint names to fit within Postgres's 63-byte identifier limit, with the migration and the schema's unique_constraint/3 agreeing on the same short name), re-clearing SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER, BEFORE spending TEST-RUNNER cycles on a run of the full suite that will reproducibly fail for this well-understood, already-diagnosed reason. This is not a request for TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to fix the code -- it is a heads-up so the next gate isn't surprised by failures that are known, understood, and not this step's fault.
